top_choice_rationale: P001 credits targeted protein degradation as one coherent achievement: bifunctional molecules form a ternary complex with measurable, tunable cooperativity and turn binding into removal of the target via an E3 ligase. The principle is independently reproduced across many ligases and laboratories, and it changes what chemists and clinicians can do against proteins without a classical pocket. Crews and Deshaies conceived the concept and Ciulli supplied the VHL ligand chemistry and structural rules that made it rational, so the allocation fits. The main weaknesses are that no degrader is a verified approved drug and that the cereblon glue strand is left out. I accept both because the citation is worded around induced proximity. P002 follows because it keeps the core PROTAC pioneers and adds base editing, which is a strong chemical-biology tool, but it drops Ciulli and splits the prize. P003 is mature but sits close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize. No award is last.
